audit.title: Price Feeds

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens with a liftable sentence — "Chainlink Data Feeds provide data that is aggregated from many data sources by a decentralized set of independent node operators." But it answers *Data Feeds*, not *Price Feeds* (the page's own title), leaving the implied question unanswered in the first chunk.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean H1/H2, no level skips, tight "What's next" list. Fine for its size, but only 2 sections means little retrievable surface.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 0 numerals, vague quantifiers "many"/"some". No mention of typical decimals (8), heartbeat/deviation thresholds, number of feeds, or supported networks.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 6 internal links to relevant concept/reference pages — good hub linking. 0 external/primary sources; acceptable for a hub but no authoritative anchor.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: The Data Feeds sentence is quotable; there is no crisp one-sentence definition of a Price Feed itself.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Strong — valid `TechArticle` + `BreadcrumbList`, canonical URL, `inLanguage`, full og/twitter set. Deductions: `datePublished`==`dateModified` (no genuine freshness signal), auto-templated `about` ("Content about using/data/feeds") and stopword-laden `keywords`.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code. Defensible for a hub, but the page's own description ("how to use … in your smart contracts") invites a minimal read example.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Low. Doesn't address "what is a price feed," "how do I read a price feed," "how often do feeds update," or error/symptom phrasings; it defers everything to child pages.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed beyond disambiguating Data Feeds vs Price Feeds.

audit.summary: This is a thin concept-hub stub (110 words, 2 sections, 0 code, 0 numerals) whose main job is to route readers to `using-data-feeds`, `historical-data`, addresses, and API reference. Its biggest strength is clean metadata and a serviceable opening definition; its biggest weakness is that a page titled "Price Feeds" never defines a *price feed* specifically and carries zero concrete specifics (decimals, heartbeat, deviation threshold, network/feed counts) — exactly the quantitative facts generative engines lift. As-is it will be outranked on "what is a Chainlink Price Feed" queries by pages that state the fact concretely, and it barely covers the symptom/how-to queries users actually type.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical one-sentence definition of "Price Feed" as the first liftable line
recommendations.where: Immediately under the `# Price Feeds` H1, before the current Data Feeds sentence.
recommendations.issue: Page titled "Price Feeds" opens with a *Data Feeds* definition; no price-feed definition exists.
recommendations.change: Add e.g. "A Chainlink Price Feed is an on-chain contract that reports the aggregated market price of an asset pair (e.g. ETH/USD), updated by a decentralized network of node operators and readable via the `AggregatorV3Interface.latestRoundData()` function."
recommendations.why: Gives engines a self-contained answer to "what is a Chainlink Price Feed" in the first chunk, resisting parametric-prior substitution.

recommendations.title: Inject concrete specifics
recommendations.change: State typical facts: price feeds return values with 8 decimals (some pairs use 18), update on a deviation threshold or heartbeat, and are live across major EVM networks — link to the addresses page for the exact list. Replace "many data sources" with a concrete count/range where known.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation; qualitative-only prose underperforms.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/how-to phrased subheadings
recommendations.issue: Content matches concept titles, not the questions devs type.
recommendations.change: Add short H2/H3s like "How do I read the latest price?", "How often do Price Feeds update?", "Price Feed vs Data Feed — what's the difference?", each with a 1–2 sentence answer that links to the deep-dive page.
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal runnable read example
recommendations.where: Under a "How do I read the latest price?" heading.
recommendations.issue: 0 code blocks on a page describing smart-contract usage.
recommendations.change: Include a short Solidity snippet calling `latestRoundData()` on `AggregatorV3Interface` with imports and a labeled network, or explicitly one-line-defer to `using-data-feeds` with the canonical function named inline.
recommendations.why: Agents extract the canonical API; naming `latestRoundData()` here blocks generic-substitute answers.

recommendations.title: Fix freshness and templated schema fields
recommendations.issue: `dateModified` equals `datePublished`; `about` entries are auto-templated ("Content about using"); `headline` is "Using Data Feeds" on a page titled "Price Feeds".
recommendations.change: Stamp a real `dateModified` on edits; replace `about` with meaningful entities ("Chainlink Price Feeds", "AggregatorV3Interface", "Data Feeds"); align `headline` with the page title.
recommendations.why: Accurate entities and visible freshness raise E-E-A-T and entity resolution; low effort, modest lift.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers ("many data sources", "some exceptions") with no numbers.
Title/content mismatch: "Price Feeds" page whose body and schema `headline` describe generic Data Feeds.
offPageNotes: Site-level: ensure `llms.txt` and sitemap list this hub and its children so the canonical-hub pattern is discoverable.
Freshness cadence is a site-generator concern — the identical timestamps suggest generator-stamped dates rather than genuine revision tracking.
The CLI should pass raw `<head>`/full rendered body; the extremely low word count is consistent with a stub, but confirm no content was truncated before treating query-coverage gaps as final.
